subject: GPU pool onboarding readiness & mutual milestones for Helix Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@helixhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU pool onboarding readiness & initial MAP for Helix Health

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I’m sharing a short mutual action plan (attached: MAP_v1.3.pdf) that ties evaluation milestones to the reservation timelines we discussed. Quick summary here to align on expectations before I send the formal MAP:  

- Objective: Reserve capacity and validate performance for Helix Health’s inference workload (clinical summarization + search re-rank) ahead of a Q3 pilot.
- Recommended initial reservation (sizing estimate): 30 x NVIDIA H100 80GB-equivalent GPUs split as: Dedicated pool (hosted) 10 GPUs for immediate throughput needs; Private on-prem tranche 20 GPUs for data residency + production cutover.
- Acceptance gating: Canary (5% traffic) -> Staggered ramp to 25% -> Full production. Acceptance criteria (measurable): p95 gen latency <250ms at 512-token context for 75% of requests during 25% traffic window; sustained token throughput target 600k tokens/min across pool; quality regressions <2% vs baseline eval set.
- Lead times: Dedicated reservation (hosted) can be provisioned in ~3–4 weeks once contract signed; Private/on-prem procurement + rack scheduling typically 12–14 weeks (procurement + rack/cabling + on-site validation).
- MAP asks for Helix: sign-off on sizing and target SLA window, confirmation of procurement PO timeline (if doing on-prem tranche), and a preferred canary week.

I’ve attached a sizing workbook that models throughput and cost at different quantization profiles. If you’re good with this direction I’ll convert MAP_v1.3 into a tracked DocuSign and propose milestone dates.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v1.3.pdf, gpu_sizing_model_v2.xlsx

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@helixhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU pool onboarding readiness & initial MAP for Helix Health

Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock sizing and the MAP:  

1) For the acceptance gating, can you add an availability SLA delta for the canary period (we need a 99.5% availability target for user-facing endpoints during the 25% ramp)?
2) The private tranche lead time is a concern for procurement — can Redwood provide a temporary burst plan so we can start pilot from hosted Dedicated capacity while on-prem is being installed?
3) Can you outline the on-site validation checklist — our infra team wants to make sure network egress, HSM/KMS integration, and audit logging are validated before we accept nodes.

If you can fold those items into the MAP (and include an indicative DocuSign timeline), I’ll route to procurement and infra. Tentatively our preferred canary week is 2027-06-14.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee | Head of AI Platform, Helix Health
samantha@helixhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-9987

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: GPU pool onboarding readiness & initial MAP for Helix Health — internal next steps

Folks — forwarding Samantha’s questions. Proposed responses and owners below (please comment if anything needs to change):

1) Availability SLA during canary (owner: Vanessa)
   - Proposal: 99.5% availability target during canary; measure at the route-level with 1-min aggregations; fallback policy: if availability drops below 98.0% for >10m, auto-roll back to previous model variant and open incident.

2) Temporary burst plan (owner: Marissa)
   - Proposal: Provide a Dedicated-hosted burst pool (up to +8 H100-equivalent vGPUs) for initial pilot. Bill as short-term usage at committed rate with 30-day elasticity. Provision path: immediate (3–5 business days after DocuSign) using reserved spare capacity.

3) On-site validation checklist (owner: Karthik) — attach canary-run-checklist.md to MAP. Key items: KMS/HSM handshake (AKV/KMS audit entries), outbound egress rule validation, time sync, NVLink/cabling verification, firewall/NAT traversal test, KV cache warm-up test (3 warm-up runs at 50% load), and audit log delivery to customer S3/GCS.

4) Sizing rationale (owner: Ben)
   - We modelled Helix’s queries at median 120 tokens/query and 1.4 qps per user (spiky over 10x). 30 H100s gives initial headroom for concurrency with sustained throughput headroom to 800k tokens/min before adding the next tranche. We recommend a safety buffer of 20% for the first 90 days to avoid throttling.

5) Milestone sketch & dates (high level - to propose to customer):
   - 2027-04-15: Final MAP & DocuSign issued (Owner: Ben)
   - 2027-04-22: DocuSign returned / PO in flight (Customer)
   - 2027-05-05: Dedicated burst pool provisioned (Hosted) (Owner: Marissa)
   - 2027-06-01: On-prem rack delivery window opens (Procurement/Infra)
   - 2027-06-14: Canary week (customer-requested) — 5% -> 25% ramp (Owner: Karthik)
   - 2027-07-01: Production full roll (contingent on pass)

Please review the attached canary checklist and the sizing workbook before I send the DocuSign. We should be conservative on the on-prem lead time in the MAP (12–14 wks). Any objections?

Thanks —
Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@helixhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Finalized MAP + DocuSign (RDW-4372) — canary week 2027-06-14

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. I’ve updated the MAP to include: availability SLA during canary (99.5% target, rollback triggers), the temporary Dedicated burst plan, and the on-site validation checklist (attached). The DocuSign for RDW-4372 is live here: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/RDW-4372-commit  — I’ve also attached the final MAP_v1.3.pdf for your records.

Key commitments in this MAP:  
- Dedicated burst pool: up to +8 H100-equivalent GPUs available within ~3–5 business days after sign (for pilot).
- Private on-prem tranche: estimated 12–14 week lead time from PO to acceptance; Redwood will provide pre-canned runbooks and an on-site playbook for rack acceptance.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 gen latency <250ms (512 tokens) during 25% ramp, 99.5% availability during canary window, and audit/log delivery validated to customer bucket.

Next steps:  
1) Please countersign DocuSign and indicate PO timing so we can schedule rack delivery and prioritize the burst pool.
2) Infra contact: Erik Johnson (erik.j@acmelabs.ai) — I looped him per your request to help coordinate procurement and on-site validation.

If that looks good I’ll plan to have Marissa spin up the burst pool once we have DocuSign returned.

Best —
Ben
